one_liner: Git hosting and collaboration platform for source code, issues, pull requests, and CI/CD via Actions.
self_serve_evidence: Any account holder can create a personal access token or register an OAuth/GitHub App directly from developer settings with no vendor approval step.
api_surface: REST API (v3) with thousands of endpoints spanning repos, issues, PRs, Actions, orgs, etc., plus a GraphQL API (v4); one of the broadest developer APIs available.
existing_mcp_detail: github/github-mcp-server — GitHub's official MCP server (also listed in the github.com/mcp registry).
notes: Username/password auth is explicitly disallowed; fine-grained PATs and GitHub Apps are the recommended modern auth paths.

one_liner: Frontend cloud platform for building, deploying, and scaling web applications (especially Next.js).
self_serve_evidence: Any authenticated user can self-generate a bearer auth token via POST /v3/user/tokens from account settings, no approval required.
api_surface: REST API covering deployments, projects, domains, teams, env vars, access groups, and integrations, documented via an OpenAPI spec at openapi.vercel.sh; broad.
existing_mcp_detail: Vercel MCP, official remote MCP server at https://mcp.vercel.com with OAuth-based client authorization.
notes: MCP supports both public (unauthenticated) doc-search tools and authenticated project/deployment management tools.

one_liner: Platform for building, deploying, and hosting web apps and static sites with integrated CI/CD.
self_serve_evidence: Any account holder can generate a Personal Access Token from Applications settings with no approval workflow.
api_surface: REST API (OpenAPI-documented at open-api.netlify.com) covering sites, deploys, forms, DNS/SSL, env vars, and teams; comprehensive.
existing_mcp_detail: netlify/netlify-mcp (@netlify/mcp package) — Netlify's official MCP server for deploying and managing sites via AI agents.
notes: OAuth2 is required specifically for building public third-party integrations others can install; PATs suffice for direct/agent use.

one_liner: Global edge network providing CDN, DNS, security (WAF/Zero Trust), and serverless compute (Workers).
self_serve_evidence: Any account holder can create scoped API Tokens (or legacy Global API Keys) directly from the dashboard without approval.
api_surface: Exclusively REST, roughly 2,500 endpoints across DNS, Workers, R2, KV, D1, Zero Trust/Access, WAF, Load Balancing, Stream, Images, AI Gateway, and more — very broad.
existing_mcp_detail: cloudflare/mcp — official token-efficient MCP server for the entire Cloudflare API, hosted at mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp using a search+execute code-mode pattern.
notes: Given the API's size, Cloudflare's own MCP avoids exposing thousands of individual tool schemas by using a query/execute pattern instead.

one_liner: Open-source backend-as-a-service providing a managed Postgres database, auth, storage, and edge functions.
self_serve_evidence: Any account holder can manually generate a Personal Access Token from their account page for immediate Management API use.
api_surface: Management/Admin REST API covering orgs, projects, database config, auth, storage, edge functions, and analytics, plus a separate auto-generated per-project PostgREST data API; broad.
existing_mcp_detail: Supabase MCP Server (supabase.com/docs/guides/ai-tools/mcp), officially maintained; also documented MCP OAuth authentication flow for connecting agents.
notes: Two distinct APIs exist: the Management API (project/org admin) and each project's own PostgREST data API (uses anon/service_role API keys).

one_liner: Native graph database platform for storing and querying highly connected data via the Cypher query language.
self_serve_evidence: Aura free-tier instances and Aura API OAuth credentials are self-serve, but Enterprise/on-prem Cypher access typically relies on admin-provisioned username/password credentials.
api_surface: No single broad public REST management API like the other apps; primary data access is Cypher over the Bolt protocol via drivers, with an HTTP Query API and a separate Aura Admin (REST) API for cloud instance lifecycle management — narrower and more fragmented than typical SaaS admin APIs.
existing_mcp_detail: neo4j/mcp — Neo4j's official MCP server (Go-based), documented at neo4j.com/docs/mcp with HTTP Bearer/Basic auth support.
blocker: No single broad self-serve REST/HTTP data API — core interaction is via Bolt-protocol drivers rather than simple HTTP calls, and Aura cloud-management is a separate API from data-plane Cypher access.
notes: Confirmed MCP auth (Basic for Community, Bearer/SSO for Aura/Enterprise) directly from docs; did not independently fetch Aura Admin API auth specifics, so self-serve nuance for cloud provisioning is medium confidence.

one_liner: Cloud data platform (data warehouse) for storing, querying, and sharing structured and semi-structured data at scale.
self_serve_evidence: A Snowflake account (including a self-serve free trial) is easy to get, but key-pair/OAuth/workload-identity auth setup for API access typically requires ACCOUNTADMIN-level configuration.
api_surface: Multiple REST API families — the SQL API (execute statements), object-management REST APIs (databases, warehouses, users), and Cortex APIs — broad in total but fragmented rather than one unified surface.
existing_mcp_detail: Snowflake's official Cortex Agents MCP Server; the earlier community Snowflake-Labs/mcp repo is now deprecated in favor of it.
blocker: Auth setup (key-pair generation, OAuth integration, or workload identity federation) generally requires admin-role configuration, and using the API requires a running (billed) virtual warehouse.
notes: Programmatic Access Tokens (PATs) are the simplest self-serve bearer-token option; JWT/key-pair and WIF are more enterprise-oriented.

one_liner: Fully managed cloud database service for MongoDB, handling cluster provisioning, scaling, and operations.
self_serve_evidence: Any Atlas org owner can self-generate API keys or OAuth2 service-account credentials directly from project/org settings, no vendor approval needed.
api_surface: Atlas Administration API (REST, OpenAPI-documented) covering clusters, backups, database users, alerts, billing, and org/project management; broad but infra-only — it explicitly does not expose the data plane.
existing_mcp_detail: MongoDB MCP Server (official, docs.mongodb.com/docs/mcp-server), supports both Atlas administration and data queries/exploration.
blocker: The Admin API manages infrastructure only, not database contents — reading/writing actual data requires a separate MongoDB wire-protocol driver connection with its own auth, not simple REST calls.
notes: OAuth2 Service Accounts (client-credentials flow) are now recommended over legacy API keys, which use HTTP Digest authentication.

one_liner: Cloud monitoring and observability platform for infrastructure, application performance, and log data.
self_serve_evidence: Any account holder can generate API and Application keys directly from account settings, with no approval workflow described in the docs.
api_surface: REST API (v1/v2) covering monitors, dashboards, metrics, logs, incidents, security signals, and APM configuration; very broad, hundreds of endpoints.
existing_mcp_detail: Datadog MCP Server (official, docs.datadoghq.com/bits_ai/mcp_server/), bridging observability data to MCP-compatible AI agents; a separate Code Security MCP server also exists.
notes: Requires two distinct credentials — an API key (write/report) and an Application key (read/full access) — passed together, rather than a single token.

one_liner: Application error tracking and performance monitoring platform for developers.
self_serve_evidence: Users can self-generate auth tokens (personal or internal-integration tokens) or register OAuth2 apps directly from account/org settings with no approval step.
api_surface: REST API covering issues, events, projects, organizations, releases, and alerts; broad and well documented.
existing_mcp_detail: getsentry/sentry-mcp — Sentry's official MCP server, positioned as middleware over the Sentry API for coding agents like Claude Code and Cursor.
notes: Also supports RFC 8628 device authorization flow for CLI/headless clients; legacy Basic-Auth API keys are deprecated for new accounts in favor of tokens/OAuth2.
